title: 3.1.5 Lab: Fix the Syntax and the Name
description: Take a broken function header — missing parentheses, wrong-case name — and fix both problems. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Fix the header
steps.instructions: The starter's function header is missing something every function header needs. Add it.

steps.title: Fix the name
steps.instructions: A capitalized name is not a syntax error, but it breaks convention. Rename the function to camelCase: showTotal.

steps.title: Call it
steps.instructions: Add a call to showTotal() after the definition so the body actually runs.

requirements.title: showTotal defined, camelCase, with parentheses
requirements.description: Code defines a function named showTotal (not ShowTotal) with an empty parameter list. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: Names in this course start with a lowercase letter and capitalise each new word. Check the spelling and the empty ( ).

requirements.title: prints the total
requirements.description: The function body logs the total. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: Inside the braces, one console.log should print the total with the number 42 in it.

requirements.title: showTotal is called
requirements.description: Code calls showTotal() as a statement. Help: 3.1.2 (Defining & Calling a Function)
requirements.hint: A call is the name plus parentheses, and the line ends with a semicolon. Add it below the function.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.1.5 Lab: Fix the Syntax and the Name". The task they were given: The starter's function header is missing something every function header needs. Add it. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
